options: It combines the patellofemoral and the femorotibial joints in the same capsule
The femorotibial joint is a ginglymus
It is a large, superficial, weight-bearing joint
The patellofemoral joint is bicondylar
It includes the proximal tibiofibular joint in its capsule
questions.explanation: The knee = patellofemoral (ginglymus) + bicondylar femorotibial joint in one capsule. The tibiofibular joint is not part of it. Also false: "The patellofemoral joint is bicondylar"; "The femorotibial joint is a ginglymus".

questions.stem: The patellar surface of the femur:
options: Has a medial slope more extensive than the lateral slope
Has a lateral slope more extensive than the medial slope
Articulates with the tibial plateau
Is on the anterior face of the distal femoral epiphysis
Articulates with the posterior face of the patella
questions.explanation: Its lateral slope is the more extensive one; the tibial plateau faces the condyles and menisci.

questions.stem: The posterior surface of the patella:
options: Is entirely articular
Is articular in its upper 2/3
Corresponds to the patellar surface of the femur
Receives the patellar ligament
Articulates with the tibial plateau
questions.explanation: Only its upper 2/3 is articular; the patellar ligament attaches to the apex.

options: Are interposed between the femoral condyles and the superior tibial articular surfaces
Are made of hyaline cartilage
Are intra-articular, semilunar fibrocartilages
The medial meniscus is "O"-shaped
Decrease the concavity of the tibial glenoids
questions.explanation: Medial = C-shaped, lateral = O-shaped. Also false: "Decrease the concavity of the tibial glenoids"; "Are made of hyaline cartilage".

options: Thickens anteriorly to form the condylar shells
Has an anterior window for the patella
Adheres laterally to the cruciate ligaments
Is cylindrical and inserts close to the articular cartilage
Has a posterior window for the patella
questions.explanation: The patellar window is anterior; posteriorly the capsule forms the condylar shells. Also false: "Adheres laterally to the cruciate ligaments"; "Thickens anteriorly to form the condylar shells".

options: An inconstant sesamoid bone in the lateral condylar shell
A meniscus
Another name for the patella
A tibial spine
A constant bone in the medial condylar shell
questions.explanation: The lateral condylar shell contains an inconstant sesamoid bone, the fabella.

questions.stem: About the collateral ligaments of the knee:
options: Their injury gives abnormal medial or lateral gapping (laxity)
The tibial collateral ligament is epiphyseal–epiphyseal
The fibular collateral ligament is epiphyseal–diaphyseal
They ensure the lateral (collateral) stability of the knee
Their injury gives a drawer sign
questions.explanation: The drawer sign is due to cruciate ligament injury (central pivot). Also false: "The tibial collateral ligament is epiphyseal–epiphyseal"; "The fibular collateral ligament is epiphyseal–diaphyseal".

questions.stem: A footballer's knee shows an abnormal forward sliding of the tibia under the femur on examination (anterior drawer). Which structure is injured?
options: The tibial collateral ligament
The patellar ligament
The arcuate ligament
The fibular collateral ligament
The anterior cruciate ligament
questions.explanation: The central pivot (cruciate ligaments) ensures anteroposterior stability; ACL rupture gives anterior drawer/laxity, PCL rupture posterior drawer.

options: Ends on the medial surface of the lateral condyle
Runs posteriorly and laterally
Arises from the posterior intercondylar area
Ends on the lateral surface of the medial condyle
Arises from the anterior intercondylar area
questions.explanation: The posteromedial cruciate arises from the posterior intercondylar area and ends on the lateral surface of the medial condyle.

questions.stem: The sagittal ligament system of the knee includes:
options: Anteriorly, the patellar ligament from the patellar apex to the anterior tibial tuberosity
The menisco-patellar ligaments only
The tibial collateral ligament
Posteriorly, the arcuate ligament fanning from the fibular head
The cruciate ligaments
questions.explanation: Sagittal system = patellar ligament (front) and arcuate ligament (back). Cruciates = central pivot; collaterals = collateral system.

questions.stem: About the patellar retinacula and menisco-patellar ligaments:
options: The lateral retinaculum is the stronger one
Menisco-patellar ligaments connect the patella to the menisci
The patellar retinacula connect the patella to each epicondyle
The medial retinaculum is wider and stronger than the lateral one
The retinacula connect the patella to the tibial spines
questions.explanation: The medial patellar wing is the wider and stronger one.

questions.stem: The extensor system of the knee is composed of:
options: The quadriceps tendon
The popliteus muscle
The patellar tendon (ligament)
The quadriceps muscle
The patella
questions.explanation: Popliteus is a posterior active stabilizer, not part of the extensor system.

questions.stem: The muscles of the "pes anserinus" (goose foot), medial active stabilizers of the knee, are:
options: Sartorius
Semitendinosus
Gracilis
Biceps femoris
Semimembranosus
questions.explanation: Pes anserinus = sartorius, gracilis, semitendinosus. Semimembranosus and biceps femoris are posterior stabilizers.

questions.stem: The synovium of the knee forms anteriorly a large recess called:
options: The acetabular recess
The quadriceps recess (cul-de-sac)
The popliteal recess
The annular recess
The olecranon recess
questions.explanation: In front, the synovium forms the large quadriceps cul-de-sac.

options: In the reference position, the leg axis continues the thigh axis
Active extension reaches 30° beyond the reference position
Passive flexion (squatting) reaches 140°
Active flexion reaches 120° with the hip flexed
Active flexion reaches 120° with the hip extended
questions.explanation: Extension is locked: it only exists from a flexed position back to the reference position. Also false: "Active flexion reaches 120° with the hip flexed"; "Passive flexion (squatting) reaches 140°".

questions.stem: What is the range of active knee flexion with the hip flexed?
questions.explanation: Active flexion: 140° hip flexed, 120° hip extended; passive flexion (squatting): 160°.

options: Medial rotation has a larger range than lateral rotation
Lateral rotation brings the toes outward by 40°
The reference position is knee flexed at 90° with the toes pointing forward
Medial rotation brings the toes inward by 30°
Rotations are measured with the knee fully extended
questions.explanation: Rotations are measured knee flexed at 90°; lateral (40°) exceeds medial (30°).

questions.stem: About the pathology of the knee:
options: Gonarthrosis is an infectious disease
MRI with or without arthrography can analyse menisci and ligaments
The most frequent traumatic lesion in athletes is the meniscal lesion
Knee dislocations are the most frequent traumatic lesion
Gonarthrosis (osteoarthritis) is frequent in older people
questions.explanation: Meniscal lesions are the most frequent; gonarthrosis is degenerative.
